name: TX-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +29 partisan lean
Incumbent Menefee running with large fundraising and outside support
Republican opponent has minimal reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: The district's +29 Democratic lean, an incumbent Democrat with over $3.6 million raised and heavy outside backing, and markets pricing a Democratic win at 96% all point to a safe Democratic hold. No polling or expert ratings contradict that picture.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of outside spending against Menefee would be the first sign of trouble.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-18 is a heavily Democratic Houston-area seat, with a partisan lean of about 29 points toward Democrats. Incumbent Christian Menefee is running for a full term and has raised more than $3.6 million, backed by roughly $7 million in outside support and no recorded opposition spending. Republican Ronald Whitfield shows little reported fundraising or infrastructure.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the race rests on fundamentals, and those fundamentals point firmly to the incumbent. Prediction markets put the Democratic win chance around 96%. The forecast is a Safe Democratic hold with a margin near 29 points.
